strengths: Addresses important practical problem of anytime NAS for tabular data with clear cloud-resource-budget motivation
NAS-Bench-Tabular benchmark with 160K architectures is a valuable contribution for future research
Comprehensive empirical evaluation of 9 existing zero-cost proxies on tabular data, demonstrating ExpressFlow superiority
Two-phase system design is well-motivated and clearly formulated with explicit time allocation constraints
Strong experimental results showing significant speedups (up to 82.75x) and consistent anytime capability
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, extensive ablations (Appendices D-F), promised code release
Thorough theoretical analysis of ExpressFlow combining trainability and expressivity considerations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: filtering phase uses standard Regularized Evolution, refinement uses standard Successive Halving, ExpressFlow combines existing concepts; primary contribution is engineering combination
Narrow evaluation scope: only 3 binary classification datasets, no regression/multi-class tasks, limited to simple fully-connected architectures (L=4 fixed), search space of 160K is modest

Insufficient theoretical justification for key design choices: K_l/ℓ(z_l) weighting appears ad-hoc, neuron saliency vs parameter saliency justification weak, data-agnostic property requiring artificial all-one vectors is questionable
Limited transferability evidence: ExpressFlow only evaluated on 3 similar tabular datasets; image data results (Table 15) show it ranks 2nd not 1st, raising generalization concerns
Weak baseline comparisons: one-shot NAS uses only basic weight-sharing (SRCC 0.12), TabNAS comparison in Table 11 shows small gaps, missing recent NAS method comparisons
Coordinator design lacks theoretical grounding: M/K≈30 and U=2 determined empirically, no explanation for why these values work; objective function is constraint-based not optimization-based
Statistical rigor issues: results report medians without confidence intervals; no discussion of variance across seeds; batch size stability (Appendix D) unexplained
Missing critical ablations: no clear isolation of filtering phase, refinement phase, and coordinator contributions; Table 11 compares only filtering+refinement combination
